niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
competitors_mentioned: James Hollis and Polly Young-Eisendrath. It
answer_verbatim:
Here are strong options, depending on what you mean by “shadow work” and the kind of spiritual practice you want:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A broad introduction featuring ten depth-psychology teachers, including James Hollis and Polly Young-Eisendrath. It covers personal and collective shadow, relationships, dreams, and practical exercises. About eight hours of video/audio lessons; a good pick if you want several perspectives.
- **[Encounters with the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/courses)** — A more focused introduction to Jung’s concept of the shadow, taught by Jungian analyst James Hollis. Look for it in the course catalog.
- **[Shadow Work — Jungian Center for the Spiritual Sciences](https://jungian.directory/courses/shadow-work/)** — A shorter independent-study workshop with audio lectures, readings, and exercises. The listing describes four sessions and a $75 cost; check the current price and availability before enrolling.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Mindfulness: What It Is, Where It Comes From, and How to Practice It — Naropa University / The Awake Network](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — A free introduction to mindfulness, including its Buddhist roots and practices for daily life.
- **[Mindworks online mindfulness courses](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/mindfulness-courses/)** — Self-paced courses with guided meditations, readings, and reflection. The progressive path starts with a free fundamentals level; teachings draw on Buddhist wisdom without requiring Buddhist terminology or religious commitment.
- **[The Power of Awareness — Sounds True](https://www.soundstrue.com/collections/meditation)** — A seven-week mindfulness course with Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield, aimed at building a regular meditation practice.
- **[Tara Brach’s Radical Compassion Institute](https://courses.tarabrach.com/)** — Self-paced courses on mindfulness and compassion, including RAIN, a practice for meeting difficult emotions with awareness and care.

**My quick picks:** For a substantial, multi-teacher shadow-work course, try *Engage the Shadow*. For a gentle, practical start to meditation, try Mindworks or Naropa’s free course. If you want to combine the two, pair a shadow-work course with a steady mindfulness practice rather than treating intense self-exploration as a substitute for meditation or therapy.

Shadow work can bring up painful memories or strong emotions. Start gradually, skip exercises that feel destabilizing, and consider working with a licensed mental-health professional if you have significant trauma or distress. Course formats, prices, and availability can change, so verify details on the provider’s site.
